## Seed-paired sensitivity (secondary; never substituted for Welch)

Seeds are shared across arms, so each seed gives one paired difference. B redraws its 1000 images at every seed while C10, CSHUF and CINV use one fixed set, so a B-vs-C difference carries set-sampling variance that a C-vs-C difference does not; pairing removes seed effects common to both arms but cannot remove that asymmetry.
